newsitem.title: USA: Swiss Army knife could've killed Nicole Simpson - ABC. [CORRECTED 00:38 GMT 19/2]
newsitem.headline: Swiss Army knife could've killed Nicole Simpson - ABC. [CORRECTED 00:38 GMT 19/2]

text.p: Former Los Angeles police detective Mark Fuhrman says he found an empty Swiss Army knife box at O.J. Simpson's home and forensic experts say it could have contained the knife that killed Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman, ABC television said on Tuesday.

Fuhrman, in a report to be shown on Wednesday night on ABC's "PrimeTime Live," said that when he visited Simpson's Brentwood estate the night Simpson's ex-wife and her friend were murdered, he discovered an empty Swiss Army knife box in a bathroom at Simpson's house and told other detectives about it.
Detective Philip Vannatter said he never saw the box, and when ABC described the box to him, he doubted whether its blades were long enough to have caused the wounds.

But ABC said it had the kind of knife contained in the box tested by four forensic experts who said it could have been the murder weapon because its blades were consistent with the type of wounds and scrape marks found on the two bodies.
Among the experts were Dr. Werner Spitz, the author of a textbook on knife wounds, who said the blade would have caused wounds deeper than its length because of compression of flesh in a victim.
The Swiss Army knife also has a serrated blade whose markings were simliar to those found on Goldman's right cheek, ABC said.
Fuhrman, the most controversial police figure in the case, broke a two-year silence to write a book in which he accuses Los Angeles police of botching the investigation by missing obvious clues.
He said he saw a bloody fingerprint at the scene of the crime, something Vannatter and his associate, Tom Lange, deny was there.
After the criminal trial, Fuhrman pleaded no contest (corrects plea from guilty) to perjury for denying under oath that he had used racial slurs in the last 10 years.

Simpson was found not guilty at his criminal trial in October 1995 of the murders, but a civil court jury last month held him liable for the deaths and ordered him to pay $33 million in various damages.
